from.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle derived mapping-complex comparison before the inverse limit: Infinity-categorical monadicity and the augmented counit bar resolution. Supporting foundation: Free coherent monad modules and their augmented free resolution. Supporting lemma: Coherent two-sided bar from a bimodule and a left module. Operadic Segal encoding of composable bimodules, before forming or realizing any bar. Supporting input: Replace the ordered-word algebra diagram by its composable-path presentation, before gluing short paths.

title: Composable paths approximate the operad of ordered bimodule words
statement:
Use the universes, ordinary nerves, quasicategories and coherent functor categories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and inert arrows and relative mapping-space Segal products of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. A planar infinity operad is an inner fibration $p:\mathcal X^\otimes\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ admitting cocartesian lifts of inert arrows, with fiber equivalences $\mathcal X_{[n]}^\otimes\simeq(\mathcal X_{[1]}^\otimes)^n$ and the relative mapping-space product condition stated there. Only inert lifts, not lifts of all arrows, are required.

For an integer $k\geq0$ let $\mathsf W_k$ be the ordinary planar coloured operad with colours $(i,j)$, $0\leq i\leq j\leq k$, $j-i\leq1$. An operation from a nonempty ordered list $((i_1,j_1),\ldots,(i_r,j_r))$ to $(i,j)$ exists uniquely when $i_1=i$, $j_r=j$ and $j_t=i_{t+1}$ for $1\leq t<r$, and is absent otherwise. A nullary operation into $(i,j)$ exists uniquely if $i=j$. Substitution concatenates these paths. Its operator category $\mathsf W_k^\otimes$ has finite ordered colour lists as objects; over the opposite of $h:[m]\to[n]$, a morphism from $(c_1,\ldots,c_n)$ to $(d_1,\ldots,d_m)$ chooses an operation $(c_{h(t-1)+1},\ldots,c_{h(t)})\to d_t$ for each $1\leq t\leq m$. Inputs outside $[h(0)+1,h(m)]$ are discarded; empty blocks use nullary operations. Composition substitutes blocks, and the functor to $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ records the lengths. Inert arrows select consecutive sublists by identity operations.

Define $\mathsf{Step}_k$ to have objects monotone maps $f:[n]\to[k]$ such that $f(t)-f(t-1)\leq1$ for $1\leq t\leq n$. A morphism $f\to g$, $g:[m]\to[k]$, is a monotone map $h:[m]\to[n]$ with $g=fh$; composition is composition of these maps in the opposite direction. Its base arrow is $[n]\to[m]$ in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, and it is marked inert when $h(t)=a+t$. There is a functor $\Phi_k:\mathsf{Step}_k\to\mathsf W_k^\otimes$ sending $f$ to the word $((f(0),f(1)),\ldots,(f(n-1),f(n)))$ and $h$ to the indicated consecutive block operations. When $h(t)=h(t-1)$ the output colour is $(f(h(t)),f(h(t)))$, with its nullary operation.

Let $\mathcal D_k(\mathcal X)$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}_{N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})}(N(\mathsf{Step}_k),\mathcal X^\otimes)$ on functors carrying marked inert edges to $p$-cocartesian edges. Define $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathsf W_k}(\mathcal X)$ in the same manner using $N(\mathsf W_k^\otimes)$. Then precomposition induces an equivalence of infinity categories $\Phi_k^*:\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathsf W_k}(\mathcal X)\to\mathcal D_k(\mathcal X)$. This equivalence includes arbitrary coherent transformations over the base and is natural under inert-preserving maps of target planar infinity operads and under inclusions of nonempty consecutive vertex intervals into $[k]$. No target colimits or presentability are assumed.

source.place: Definition 4.4.1.12 and Proposition 4.4.1.17, with the proof on printed pp. 568-570; planar form via Theorem 4.1.3.14 and the ordered-word fiber of Definition 4.4.1.1. This is the path approximation, not the Segal gluing theorem 4.4.1.11. Online 2017 source read; WANTED: archived Higher Algebra. No Stacks tag states this operadic approximation.

proof.text: Write $S=\mathsf{Step}_k$ and $O=\mathsf W_k^\otimes$. Form the ordinary mapping cylinder $J$ with full subcategories $O,S$, no arrows from $S$ to $O$, and $\operatorname{Hom}_J(w,f)=\operatorname{Hom}_O(w,\Phi_k f)$ for $w\in O,f\in S$. Composition uses $\Phi_k$. Let $i:O\hookrightarrow J$ and $r:J\to O$ be the inclusion and retraction, with $r|_S=\Phi_k$. The identity of $\Phi_k f$ gives a bridge $b_f:i\Phi_k f\to f$. These bridges, and identities on $O$, give a natural transformation $b:ir\to1_J$, with $ri=1_O$ and $rb=1_r$. Equip $J$ with its length functor to $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. All bridges lie over identity arrows. For a cross arrow $\alpha:w\to\Phi_k f$, composing with $u:w'\to w$ gives $\alpha u$, and composing with $v:f\to g$ gives $\Phi_k(v)\alpha$. The associativity equations reduce to associativity in $O$ and $S$ and functoriality of $\Phi_k$; for example $\Phi_k(v)(\alpha u)=(\Phi_k(v)\alpha)u$. Also $b_g\Phi_k(v)=v b_f$ and $b_f\alpha=\alpha$ as cross arrows, which verifies naturality on all arrow types. These formulas include empty blocks. Only ordinary categories and their nerves, as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], have been used.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.1.17, printed p. 568: mapping cylinder and retraction.

proof.text: For a word $w=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ put $K_w=S\times_J J_{w/}$. An object is a path $f:[m]\to[k]$ and an operation $\alpha:w\to\Phi_k f$ with opposite base map $h:[m]\to[n]$. Let $I_w\subset K_w$ be the full subcategory where $\alpha$ is inert, that is, $h(t)=a+t$ and the selected word is exactly the adjacent-pair word of $f$. Its objects are composable consecutive subwords of $w$; a zero-length subword at each position $a$ carries, in addition, any vertex label $v\in[k]$. Define $R(\alpha)$ by the hull interval $[h(0),h(m)]$. If it has positive length, the blocks of $\alpha$ concatenate to make this selected subword composable: endpoints match across nonempty blocks, and any intervening nullary block forces equal consecutive vertices of $f$. Its unique vertex path $d$ satisfies $d(h(t)-h(0))=f(t)$. If the hull has length zero, all blocks are empty, so $f$ is constant; use that constant vertex as its label. The shifted map $h-h(0)$ gives $R(\alpha)\to\alpha$ in $K_w$. For an inert interval object $e$ of $I_w$, a map $e\to\alpha$ exists uniquely precisely when the values of $h$ lie in its interval and its vertex path restricts to $d$. This is also precisely the condition for a map $e\to R(\alpha)$. The zero-length labelled intervals satisfy the same test. Hence $R$ is a right adjoint to $I_w\hookrightarrow K_w$, with the described counit; this Hom test also verifies its functoriality.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.1.17, printed pp. 569-570: inert factorization subcategory J2 and its right adjoint; explicit ordered-block hull.

proof.text: Fix an inert-preserving $F_0:N(S)\to\mathcal X^\otimes$ over lengths. Write $j:I_w\hookrightarrow K_w$, let $H_w:N(K_w)\to\mathcal X^\otimes$ be the diagram induced by $F_0$, and let $g_w:N(K_w)^{\triangleleft}\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ be its prescribed base cone with apex the length of $w$. For each $\alpha\in K_w$, step 2 gives a terminal object $R(\alpha)\to\alpha$ in $(I_w\downarrow\alpha)$. Its terminal arrows contract its nerve. Thus the opposite form of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-comma-criterion], using the opposite conventions of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence], applies to $N(j)$. Restriction identifies the spaces of transformations from each constant diagram to $H_w$ and to $H_wN(j)$. The same assertion holds after postcomposition by $p$, naturally in the constant source. These are the restriction maps themselves, compatible with $p$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.1.17, printed pp. 569-570: reduction from J1 to the inert full subcategory J2.

proof.text: For any particular cone $q:N(K_w)^{\triangleleft}\to\mathcal X^\otimes$, apply the limit form of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test]. In the square testing each constant source $z$, restriction to $I_w$ leaves the left mapping spaces unchanged and gives equivalences on both right mapping spaces by step 3. The squares commute, including their cone homotopies. Apply [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] to their path-pullback models, with the identity on the lower-left space. The testing square for $q$ is a homotopy pullback if and only if the one for its restriction is. Consequently $q$ is a $p$-limit diagram if and only if its restriction to $N(I_w)^{\triangleleft}$ is. This comparison assumes no other limits.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.1.17, printed pp. 569-570: reduction from J1 to the inert full subcategory J2.

proof.text: Given a $p$-limit cone $q_I:N(I_w)^{\triangleleft}\to\mathcal X^\otimes$ with boundary $H_wN(j)$ and base $g_w|_{N(I_w)^{\triangleleft}}$, apply the dual slice assertion of [lem-coef-cofinal-relative-join-slice-restriction] to $N(j)$, $H_w$, and $p$. The inclusion is full, both indexing categories are small, its commas $(I_w\downarrow\alpha)$ contract by step 3, and $p$ is inner by the operad hypothesis. The vertex $(q_I,g_w)$ of the displayed pullback therefore lifts. Unwinding its join slices gives $q:N(K_w)^{\triangleleft}\to\mathcal X^\otimes$ with $q|_{N(K_w)}=H_w$, $q|_{N(I_w)^{\triangleleft}}=q_I$ and $pq=g_w$, all exactly. Step 4 makes $q$ a $p$-limit. Restriction gives the converse. This proves the needed existence reduction with exact boundary and base; no equivalence-rectification argument is left implicit.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.1.17, printed pp. 569-570: reduction from J1 to the inert full subcategory J2.

proof.text: Let $E_w\subset I_w$ consist of the $n$ singleton-edge projections of $w$, a discrete category. An interval path of length $m$ has exactly its $m$ edge projections as its outgoing comma with $E_w$. For $m=0$ this comma is empty, including every labelled zero-length interval. The boundary diagram on $I_w$ induced by $F_0$ carries these projections to inert cocartesian edges. The relative product clause of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] makes each such projection cone a $p$-limit. To use it in the diagram sense, apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test]: over the discrete mapping sets of the base, its constant-source square is a homotopy pullback exactly when, for every base arrow $\phi$, the displayed $\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}$-to-product map is an equivalence. For $m=0$ this is the empty relative product over $[0]$. Hence this boundary diagram is a pointwise relative right Kan extension from $E_w$. The cone comparison in [lem-coef-relative-right-kan-universal-restriction] reduces its limit to $E_w$. Essential surjectivity of the fiber Segal equivalence supplies an object $x$ over $[n]$ with cocartesian singleton projections $x\to y_i$ and equivalences $y_i\simeq F_0([1]\xrightarrow{x_i}[k])$ in the fiber over $[1]$. Compose each projection with this equivalence. The mapping criterion [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] makes an equivalence over identity cocartesian, and [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] makes the composites cocartesian. Thus their targets are exactly the prescribed boundary values, and the relative product condition makes this cone the required $p$-limit over the prescribed base cone. The cone comparison extends it with the exact boundary over $I_w$, and step 5 extends it over $K_w$. For $n=0$, $E_w$ is empty; the empty relative product over $[0]$ supplies the apex even though $I_w$ contains all k+1 labelled vertex paths.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.1.17, printed p. 570: J2 to J3, followed by the operadic product; zero-output case included.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-relative-right-kan-universal-restriction] to the full inclusion $N(S)\subset N(J)$, $p:\mathcal X^\otimes\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ and the length functor. All indexing categories are small. For $w\in O$, step 6 supplies the required local relative limit. For $f\in S$, its local comma is $S_{f/}$ with initial object $1_f$. For each $\alpha:f\to g$ there is exactly one arrow $1_f\to\alpha$, so the comma for the inclusion $\{1_f\}\subset S_{f/}$ is a point. The opposite cofinal-comma criterion therefore identifies the constant-source mapping spaces for this comma diagram with those for its value $F_0(f)$ at $1_f$, in both total and base categories. The cone with apex $F_0(f)$ restricts to the identity edge, whose constant-source square is a homotopy pullback; the constant-test criterion proves that its full local cone is a relative limit. This verifies the theorem's existence hypothesis for every inert-preserving $F_0$. Moreover, the calculations show that a diagram $F$ on $J$ restricting to $F_0$ is pointwise right Kan extended exactly when, for every word $w$, its cone on the maps $\beta_i:w\to f_i$ is the relative product cone, where $f_i:[1]\to[k]$ has colour $x_i$. Each $\beta_i$ is the singleton projection in $O$ followed by $b_{f_i}$. The 'exactly when' follows by both directions of the cone comparison in the cited theorem, the coinitial constant-test comparison in step 4, and the identity local cones at objects of $S$. Thus restriction from this full right-Kan subcategory to inert-preserving diagrams on $S$ is an equivalence, including all transformations.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.1.17, printed pp. 569-570: assertions (a) and (b prime), with full categorical restriction.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A$ be the full subcategory of diagrams $F:N(J)\to\mathcal X^\otimes$ over lengths such that $F|_O$ preserves inert arrows and every $F(b_f)$ is an equivalence. Its restriction to $S$ preserves inert arrows: $b$ gives a pointwise equivalence from $(F|_O)\Phi_k$ to $F|_S$, and the mapping-space criterion [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] is invariant under these equivalences at the two endpoints. For such $F$, each $F(\beta_i)$ is cocartesian, as a singleton inert projection followed by an equivalence over identity; the criterion just cited makes an equivalence over identity cocartesian, and [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] gives composition. The relative product axiom and constant-test comparison in step 6 now give the product criterion of step 7. Hence every $F\in\mathcal A$ is one of those right Kan extensions.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.1.17, printed p. 570: A is contained in A prime.

proof.text: Conversely let $F$ be a right Kan extension with $F|_S$ inert-preserving. For a path $f:[m]\to[k]$, step 7 identifies $F(\Phi_k f)$ as a relative product of the $m$ singleton path values. The inert projections of $f$ make $F(f)$ the same relative product. The bridge $b_f$ is a map between these cones, because $b$ is natural. The universal property [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], read through [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test], gives an inverse comparison over $1_{[m]}$ fixing the boundary: each space of comparisons over the fixed identity data is contractible, so the two composites are identities up to all coherent homotopies. Thus $F(b_f)$ is an equivalence. This includes $m=0$, where both apices lie in the point-equivalent zero fiber. For a word $w$, its maps $F(\beta_i)$ in step 7 are inert projections: compare the relative product cone to the tuple supplied by the fiber Segal equivalence, obtaining an equivalence over $1_{[n]}$ fixing the boundary: the constant-test square gives a contractible space of comparisons over the identity base cone, and applying it in both directions gives inverse comparisons. The tuple with the exact singleton targets is constructed in step 6. The mapping criterion and cocartesian composition [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] then identify these maps with cocartesian projections. Since $\beta_i=b_{f_i}\rho_i$, and the bridge images are equivalences, the images $F(\rho_i)$ of all singleton inert maps in $O$ are cocartesian as well.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.1.17, printed p. 570: essential uniqueness of the products, bridge equivalences, and singleton inert maps.

proof.text: The singleton conclusion implies preservation of every inert map $a:w\to w'$ of $O$. Choose a cocartesian lift $u:F(w)\to y$ over its base map. Initiality in the lift category, from [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], factors $F(a)$ through $t:y\to F(w')$ over identity. Write $v_j:F(w')\to z_j$ for its singleton projections from step 9, and choose cocartesian singleton projections $q_j:y\to y_j$. Initiality of $q_j$ factors $v_jt$ as $s_jq_j$, where $s_j:y_j\to z_j$ lies over identity. The map $v_jF(a)$ is the image under $F$ of $a$ followed by the $j$th singleton projection of $w'$, so is cocartesian by step 9. The map $q_ju$ is cocartesian by composition. The triangle $s_jq_ju\simeq v_jF(a)$ therefore compares two initial lifts of the same base map. Initial-lift uniqueness makes $s_j$ an equivalence. Under the Segal fiber functor of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], the $s_j$ are the components of $t$, by the defining triangles $s_jq_j\simeq v_jt$. That functor is an equivalence and hence reflects equivalences; explicitly, apply its quasi-inverse and the two natural equivalences to an inverse of the tuple $(s_j)_j$. Thus $t$ is an equivalence. For a zero-length target the empty tuple detects this in the point-equivalent fiber. The mapping criterion [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] and cocartesian composition imply that $F(a)$ is cocartesian. This proves $F\in\mathcal A$. Steps 8-10 identify the full right-Kan subcategory in step 7 with $\mathcal A$, and therefore restriction $\mathcal A\to\mathcal D_k(\mathcal X)$ is an equivalence of full infinity categories.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.1.17, printed p. 570: A prime is contained in A; detection of arbitrary inert maps.

proof.text: Restriction $i^*:\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathsf W_k}(\mathcal X)$ has inverse up to equivalence $r^*$. Indeed $i^*r^*=1$ strictly, while $F(b)$ gives a coherent transformation $r^*i^*F\to F$, natural also in transformations $F\to G$. All its components are equivalences by the definition of $\mathcal A$. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] it is a functor equivalence on diagram categories. The relative functor categories here are quasicategories by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]; the equivalence is over the fixed base diagram since $b$ is over identity. To check the inverse data over the base explicitly, the functor simplicial set into $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ is the nerve of the ordinary functor category: an $r$-simplex is a functor $J\times[r]\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, that is, a chain of natural transformations. The image of any inverse to $F(b)$ is consequently an inverse to the identity natural transformation, hence the identity. Its inverse-triangle witnesses also project to degenerate triangles, since a triangle in an ordinary nerve is determined by its edges. The inverse and its witnesses therefore belong to the strict fiber over the length diagram. Thus the equivalence is in the relative categories too. The full subcategories defining $\mathcal A$ and the algebra categories retain all these equivalences. Compose $r^*$ with the restriction equivalence of step 10. Its actual composite is precomposition by $r|_S=\Phi_k$, proving the claimed equivalence including arbitrary coherent transformations.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.1.17, printed p. 569: comparison through A; explicit deformation-retraction argument in place of the left-Kan invocation.

proof.text: The forward comparison is the actual restriction $\Phi_k^*$. Postcomposition with an inert-preserving target map commutes with it on every functor simplex. Inclusion of a nonempty consecutive vertex interval commutes with $\Phi$: both orders send each path to its list of adjacent pairs and each map to the same consecutive block operations. Hence the corresponding restriction squares commute on objects, transformations and all higher simplices. This proves both naturalities without requiring these target maps to preserve auxiliary limits. The argument includes k=0, singleton intervals, all k+1 separate length-zero paths, and nullary loop blocks. Only the relative products required by the operad axioms were used; no target colimits or presentability were assumed.
